chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was exiting from the Ka'bah, and he was saying: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,' until he had said it three times. Then he said: 'O Allah, do not overwhelm our afflictions, O our Lord, and do not let our enemies gloat over us, for indeed You are the One who causes harm and confers benefit.' Then he descended and prayed beside the stairs, placing the stairs on his left, facing the Ka'bah, with no one between him and it. Then he went out to his house.

key_terms.الدَّرَجَةِ: The stairs (leading up to the Ka'bah)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him ) do immediately after exiting the Ka'bah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual etiquette of Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) upon exiting the Ka'bah, where he recited Takbir three times and supplicated for relief from afflictions, affirming God as the sole source of harm and benefit. He then performed a voluntary prayer facing the Ka'bah with the stairs to his left, a practice that underscores the sanctity of the immediate vicinity of the sanctuary in Shia jurisprudence. This act reflects the broader theological principle of recognizing divine omnipotence in both ease and hardship, a theme central to Shia devotional practices.
